newsitem.title: GERMANY: Stability pact details worry some Germans -paper.
newsitem.headline: Stability pact details worry some Germans -paper.

text.p: One week after Germany celebrated international agreement of a stability pact to ensure fiscal restraint in Europe's planned currency union, government officials have concerns about the pact's details.
German Tagesspiegel, citing unnamed government sources, said some government officials were worried about the details of implementing the pact.
Agreements on sanctions, punishing nations whose fiscal discipline had lapsed, now needed to be turned into rules, and "there could be problems with some details," the newspaper said.

Some members of the German finance ministry interpreted the pact as containing "quasi-automatic" sanctions, the newspaper said. But European partners had argued against an automatic triggering of sanctions.
